S40.01.note: Personalization is stored for AGI Cloud answers only, per its picker placeholder; the reply check is server-side.
steps: Open the sidebar menu and click Personalization.
Click What should AGI call you? and type a name, then press Enter.
Check the row now shows that name instead of Not set.
Send a new chat message and check the reply uses that name.
S40.01.where: Sidebar > Personalization > What should AGI call you?

S40.02.note: No separate free-text background field exists; the closest is this 120-character field, so it covers Expected only partly. Custom instructions in Settings is a further free-text option.
steps: Open the sidebar menu and click Personalization.
Click What do you do? and type a short background, up to 120 characters, then press Enter.
Check the row shows that text instead of Not set.
Send a chat message that depends on that background and check the reply keeps it in mind.
S40.02.where: Sidebar > Personalization > What do you do?

S40.03.note: Tailoring of replies happens on the server; the code only stores the text.
steps: Open the sidebar menu and click Personalization.
Click What do you do? and type a role, such as a job title, then press Enter.
Check the row shows the role.
Send a question in that field of work and check the reply fits that role.
S40.03.where: Sidebar > Personalization > What do you do?

S40.05.note: Only one style can be chosen at a time, as Expected says.
steps: Open the sidebar menu and click Personalization.
Click Style, then pick Concise, Explanatory, Learning, Formal or Default.
Check the Style row shows the chosen name.
Send a question and compare the reply with the style chosen.

S40.07.note: There is no separate more or less formal control; only the Formal style option exists, so the check is partial.
steps: Open the sidebar menu and click Personalization.
Click Style and pick Formal.
Check the Style row shows Formal.
Send a question and check the reply uses a formal register.

S40.08.note: The named presets are the Style choices; the Tone section holds separate on or off traits, not presets.
steps: Open the sidebar menu and click Personalization.
Click Style and look at the named choices: Default, Concise, Explanatory, Learning, Formal.
Pick one preset, then check the Style row shows it.
Send a question and check the reply follows that one preset.

S40.09.note: Only three settings exist (Default and the two ends), not a graded scale.
steps: Open the sidebar menu and click Personalization.
Under the Tone heading, click Warmth.
Pick Warm and personable, or Neutral and businesslike, or Default.
Check the Warmth row shows the choice, then send a question and compare the tone of the reply.

S40.10.note: Only three settings exist (Default and the two ends), not a graded scale.
steps: Open the sidebar menu and click Personalization.
Under the Tone heading, click Enthusiasm.
Pick Energetic and encouraging, or Measured, or Default.
Check the Enthusiasm row shows the choice, then send a question and compare the reply.

S40.11.note: A second setting, Tone > Headers and lists, also covers this; Formatting holds the fuller choice list.
steps: Open the sidebar menu and click Personalization.
Click Formatting and pick Prose, or Headings and bullet lists, or another option.
Check the Formatting row shows the choice.
Send a question and compare whether the reply uses headings and lists or flowing prose.

S40.12.note: Only the two ends and Default exist, not a graded scale.
steps: Open the sidebar menu and click Personalization.
Under the Tone heading, click Emoji.
Pick No emoji or Emoji welcome.
Check the Emoji row shows the choice, then send a question and check whether the reply uses emoji.
Open the sidebar menu and click Personalization.
Click Technical level and pick Beginner, Intermediate or Expert.
Check the Technical level row shows the choice.
Send the same technical question and compare the depth of the reply.

S40.14.note: The language prompt is a free tag; leaving it empty returns to answering in the language the user writes in.
steps: Open the sidebar menu and click Personalization.
Click Language, type a tag such as de, then press Enter.
Check the Language row shows de.
Send a question in English and check the reply is written in German.

S40.16.note: No on or off switch exists in the code: the only way to stop them is to clear the text and save, which deletes it, so Expected's switch-off without deleting is not met. The text is stored locally, not per account.
steps: Click the Code: Open Settings command (or Sidebar > Settings).
Click Instructions & editor in the left list.
Under Custom instructions, type a standing instruction in Host default, then click Save host instructions.
Open a new chat and check the reply follows it; the Effective turn prelude box should show the text.
S40.16.where: Settings > Instructions & editor > Custom instructions > Host default

S40.17.needs: a signed-in AGI Cloud account with at least one project
S40.17.note: Project instructions are cloud data set on a project; the Instructions & editor section shows only local repository files, which are a separate source.
steps: Open the sidebar menu and click Projects, then select a project.
In the project list under Edit, click Instructions.
Type project instructions in Project instructions and press Enter.
Open a new chat in that project and check the reply follows the instructions; the Instructions row should now show Set.
S40.17.where: Sidebar > Projects > (select a project) > Edit > Instructions

steps: Open the sidebar menu and click Personalization.
Click Style and pick Explanatory.
Check the Style row shows Explanatory.
Ask a how-to question and check the reply explains the reasoning and context.

S40.26.note: Length > Shorter is a related but separate setting in the same menu.
steps: Open the sidebar menu and click Personalization.
Click Style and pick Concise.
Check the Style row shows Concise.
Ask a question and check the reply is short and direct.

S40.28.note: The header line naming the scope (this VS Code host or this VS Code workspace) comes from apps/extension-vscode/src/features/instructions/customInstructions.ts; the Context panel's Custom instructions row also shows the scope.
steps: Click the Code: Open Settings command (or Sidebar > Settings).
Click Instructions & editor in the left list.
Read the Effective turn prelude box; it shows the exact instruction block added to new turns, with its scope in the header.
Read the Runtime-discovered project sources list and compare the named sources with Expected.
S40.28.where: Settings > Instructions & editor > Effective turn prelude
